721.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. I have made one plea before you, O Creator: give it your ear. You are true, great and gracious, without flaw, the Sustainer of all. Know it for certain, O heart: the world is a place that passes away; Azrail has seized the hair of my head, and you, O heart, know nothing of it. Wife, son, father, brothers: there is none among them to take my hand; at the last, when I have fallen and the takbir (of the funeral prayer) is said, no one can keep me (here). Night and day I roamed in craving, and dwelt on thoughts of evil; never have I done a good deed; such is my state. One like me is ill-starred, a backbiter, heedless, shameless and without fear; (yet) Nanak, your servant, says to you: (may I be) the dust under the feet of your servants. ॥4॥

This shabad is in Persian: yak araj guftam pesi to (I have made one plea before you), dar gos kun (give ear), haka (true), kabir (great), karim (gracious), be-aib (without flaw), parvadgar (the Sustainer), mukame fani (a place that passes away), tahkik (for certain), dani (know), mam sar mui (the hair of my head), giraftah (seized), hechi na (nothing at all), jan pisar padar biradaran (wife, son, father, brothers), kas nes dastangir (there is none to take one's hand), biaftam (I fell), sab roj (night and day), hava (craving), gahe na (never), ahval (state), badbakhat (ill-starred), ham chu (one like me), bakhil (a backbiter), ghafil (heedless), benajar (shameless), bebak (fearless), bugoyad (says), tura (to you), pa khak (the dust of the feet).
Azrail (Azrael): in Islamic tradition, the angel of death, who takes the soul from the body. Takbir: the words Allahu akbar (God is greatest), said over the dead in the funeral prayer.
721.2: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Fear of you is my bhang, and my mind the pouch (that holds it); (drunk on it) I have become one possessed, a renunciate. My hands are my begging bowl; (my) hunger is for the sight of you; at (your) door I beg, each day and every day. I raise the beggar's cry for the sight of you; I am a beggar at (your) door: put alms (in my bowl). Saffron, flowers, musk and gold are put upon the bodies of all; the devotees are like sandalwood; such is their nature that they make all fragrant. Of ghee, silk and the vessel (of ghee) no one speaks (as defiled); such is the devotee, whatever the caste he is born in. Those who, bowed low in your Name, stay attuned to you in love: Nanak (prays): at their door, put alms (in my bowl). ॥3॥
Bhang: cannabis, which some ascetics carry in a pouch for its intoxication; kasa: the begging bowl. The shabad takes these ascetics' things to picture the beggar at the Lord's door.
721.3: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. This body has been steeped in the mordant of Maya, O beloved, and then dyed in greed; such a gown does not please my Husband; O beloved, how is the soul-bride to reach his bed? I am a sacrifice, O Merciful One, I am a sacrifice; I am a sacrifice to those who take your Name; those who take your Name, to them I am ever a sacrifice. Should the body be made the dyeing-tub, O beloved, and the madder of the Name be put in it, and should the Dyer, the Master (himself), dye it, a colour (comes) such as was never seen. Those whose gowns are so dyed, O beloved, have the Husband beside them. Would that their dust were given (to me): dear one, put this prayer of Nanak's (before them). He himself fashions, he himself dyes, he himself casts his glance of grace; O Nanak, the soul-bride who is pleasing to her Husband, he himself enjoys. ॥4॥
Pahu (mordant): the salt, alum or soda in which cloth is steeped before dyeing, so that the colour holds fast. Madder (majith): a red dye from the root of a plant, a colour that never fades.
722.1: Raag Tilang, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O foolish young (bride), why do you take such pride? In your own home, why do you not delight in the Lord's love? The Husband is near, O crazed bride; why do you search outside? Put the fear (of God) into your eyes with the needle, as kohl, and make loving devotion your adornment. Only then is she known as a happy soul-bride, joined (to him), when the Husband bestows his love (on her). What can the foolish young girl do, if the bride is not pleasing to her Husband? She may plead and lament ever so much, yet that bride does not reach the Mansion (of his presence); without (his) grace nothing is gained, however much she runs about. Drunk on craving, greed and pride, she is sunk in Maya; by these ways the Husband is not found: the bride has proved foolish. Go and ask those happy soul-brides by what ways the Husband is found. (They answer:) whatever he does, let us accept as good, and give up cleverness and the giving of our own orders; the One through whose love the treasure is gained, on his feet let us fix our mind; what the Husband says, let us do; let us give him body and mind: such is the perfume to wear. So say the happy soul-brides, O sister: by these ways the Husband is found. When the self is lost, then the Husband is found; what other cleverness (avails)? The day the Husband looks on her with grace, that day counts; the bride has gained the nine treasures. She who is dear to her Husband is the happy soul-bride; O Nanak, she is held in honour by all. Dyed in such love, drunk with Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), night and day she stays merged in love; she alone is beautiful, lovely of form and discerning; she is called wise. ॥4॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world.
722.2: Raag Tilang, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). As the Word of the Master comes to me, so do I make it known, O Lalo. Leading a wedding party of sin, (Babur) has swept in from Kabul, and demands by force the gift of a bride, O Lalo. Modesty and dharam have both gone into hiding, and falsehood goes about as the headman, O Lalo. The qazis' and the Brahmins' part is over; Satan reads the marriage, O Lalo. The Muslim women read their scriptures, and in their agony cry out to Khuda, O Lalo. Hindu women of high caste and of low, and the rest: count them too in the same reckoning, O Lalo. Wedding songs of blood are sung, O Nanak, and the saffron sprinkled is blood, O Lalo. Nanak sings the virtues of the Master in this city of corpses; speak (you too) this sure word: he who made (the world) set it to its pleasures; he sits apart, alone, and watches. True is that Master, true is his justice; true is the judgement he will give: this is the sure word. The cloth of the body will be torn to shreds, and Hindustan will remember this word. (They) come in seventy-eight and will go in ninety-seven; another man of valour will also rise. Nanak speaks the Word of the True One; he will proclaim the Truth: (this is) the time for Truth. ॥2॥

Lalo: a carpenter of Saidpur (now Eminabad), at whose home Guru Nanak stayed. This shabad is held to tell of the sack of Saidpur by Babur's army, come from Kabul. Seventy-eight and ninety-seven: the Bikrami years 1578 and 1597 (1521 and 1540 CE). Agad (aqd): the Muslim marriage contract; kungu: saffron, sprinkled at a wedding.
723.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. All have come from the Master by his Hukam (God's will and command); by his Hukam the whole (world) goes about its work. True is the Master, true is his play; everywhere the Lord is the Owner. Praise the True One: the Lord, the Owner, is above all; he has no rival: of what account am I, to reckon (his worth)? Air, water, earth and sky are the house and temple the Lord has made (for himself); within them, O Nanak, he himself is at work; tell me, what can I count as false? ॥2॥
723.2: Raag Tilang, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The one of evil mind does fruitless deeds every day, and boasts of them; when he brings home (some gain) by trickery and lies, he thinks he has won the world. Such a passing show is the world, yet he does not remember the Lord's Name; in an instant all this perishing (show) is gone: O my mind, meditate on Ram. That hour does not come to his mind, when Death, tormenting like a thorn, will come and seize him. O Nanak, the one in whose heart (the Lord), in his grace, comes to dwell, he sets free. ॥2॥
723.3: Raag Tilang, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Out of dust and light (God) has made the world and all that is in it; sky, earth, trees and water are the creation of Khuda. O man, all that the eye sees will pass away; yet the world, heedless in its craving, feeds on carrion (what is forbidden). Like ghouls and beasts it kills unlawfully and eats carrion; its heart is held fast in (craving's) grip, and the Almighty gives it the punishment of hell. The father who gave you good things, brothers, court, estates and homes: when Azrail binds you, of what use (will they be) then, at the parting? The Pure One, Allah, knows (your) every state; O Nanak, say your prayer in the presence of the dervishes, the servants (of God). ॥4॥

This shabad is in Persian: khak (dust), nur (light), kardan (made), alam (the world), jimi (earth), darakhat (trees), ab (water), paidais (creation), chasam (the eye), didan (seen), fanai (passing away), murdar (carrion, the forbidden), khurdani (eating), gaiban (unseen beings, ghouls), haivan (beasts), kustani (killing), bakhorai (eats), kabaj (grip), kadar (the Almighty), dojak (hell), vali niamat (giver of good things), milak (estates), khana (home), bastani (binding), chi kare (of what use), haval (state), bugo (say), darves (dervishes, God's own servants).
723.4: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). There is no other but you; you are the Creator: what you do, that comes to pass. Yours is the strength (we have), and in the mind is your support; O Nanak, ever and ever repeat (the Name of) the One. The Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), the Giver, is over all; (O Lord,) yours is the prop, yours the support. You alone are, and you will ever be, beyond reach, beyond fathoming, lofty and without end. Those who serve you have no fear and no pain; by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, they sing (your) praises. All that is seen is your form, O treasure of virtues, O Govind of beauty beyond compare. O servant (of God), remember, remember, remember him; O Nanak, (he) is found by (his) grace alone. I am a sacrifice to the one who has repeated (the Name); in his company the world crosses over. Says Nanak: O God, fulfil (my) longing; for the dust of the Sants' feet I long. ॥4॥
724.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Merciful is the Master, merciful; my Master is merciful. To every being he grants his gifts. Why do you falter, O mortal? The Creator will protect you. He who brought you into being gives (you) support. He who made the earth takes care of it; dwelling in every heart, he is the Master of hearts, the true Sustainer. The worth of (his) creation cannot be known; he is great, and needs no one; O man, give (him) your devotion while breath remains in your body. (O Lord,) you are all-powerful, beyond words, beyond the senses; soul and body are your capital (in our keeping). By your mercy (I) have found peace; ever (to you) is Nanak's prayer. ॥4॥
724.2: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Creator, (seeing) your creation, I long for (the sight of) you; in faith and in the world you alone (are mine); you stand untouched by all creation. In an instant you set up and pull down; wondrous are your forms. Who can know your wonders? (You are) a lamp in the darkness. You yourself are the Master of creation and of the world, O Allah, merciful Khuda; how should one who worships you day and night go to hell? Azrail is the friend of the man who has your support; all his sins are pardoned; your servants behold the sight of you. All the things of the world are for the moment only; your Name is the true peace. Meeting the Guru, Nanak has understood (this); (now) I ever sing of the One alone. ॥4॥

Persian and Arabic words: mustak (longing), din duniya (faith and the world), khalak (creation), pak (pure, untouched), yar (friend), gunah (sins), afu (pardoned), didar (sight), filhal (for the moment).
724.3: Raag Tilang, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Chief, O Wise One, Purifier of hearts, love (of you) dwells in (my) mind and body, O true King, O Freer of captives. To behold the sight of you, O Master: there is no price for it at all; you are the Pure One, the Sustainer; you yourself are the Master, great and beyond weighing. Take my hand, O Brave One; you alone, you alone are the One. O Creator, Maker of all nature, Fashioner of all beings: Nanak leans on you alone. ॥2॥

Persian words: miran (chief), danan (wise), dil soch (purifier of the heart), muhabate (love of you), bandi moch (freer of captives), didane didar (beholding the sight), dastgiri (taking the hand, help), dilavar (brave), khalak (the Creator).
724.4: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. He who made (the world) has watched over it; what can one say, O brother? He who has planted the garden himself knows, and himself acts. (Tell) the tale of the Beloved, the tale through which there is peace for ever. She who has not enjoyed her Husband in love, O brother, comes to repent; wringing her hands, she beats her head, when the night (of life) is spent. Repenting brings nothing, once (the night) is wholly gone; then the Beloved can be enjoyed only when (her) turn comes again. The happy soul-brides have won the Husband; they are better than I; those virtues do not come to me; on whom, O dear one, shall I lay the blame? I shall go and ask the friends who have enjoyed the Husband; I will fall at their feet and entreat them, and have them tell me the way. She who recognises the Hukam, O Nanak, and wears the fear (of God) as sandal, the bride who makes virtues her love-charms: then she wins the Beloved. One who has met (him) in the heart stays united; that one alone, O brother, is said to have met (him). However much one may long, there is no union by mere talk. Metal blends again with metal, and love runs to love; when (this) is understood by the Guru's grace, then one attains the Fearless (Lord). A garden of betel may grow in the home, yet the donkey knows nothing of its worth; only when one delights in fragrance does one know the flower. O Nanak, one who drinks the Amrit, his wandering doubt dies away within; in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj, he stays united, and attains the deathless state. ॥10॥
725.1: Raag Tilang, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My friend the Guru has recounted to (me) the Lord's stories and tales; I am a sacrifice to my own Guru; to the Guru I give myself. Come and meet me, O Sikh of the Guru, come and meet me, you beloved of my Guru. The Lord's praises please the Lord; these (praises) I have received from the Guru. To those who have accepted the Guru's will I am a sacrifice, again and again. I give myself to those who have seen the beloved True Guru; to those who have served the Guru I am ever a sacrifice. O Lord, Har Har, your Name is the dispeller of sorrow; it is found by serving the Guru; through the Guru comes deliverance. Those who meditate on the Lord's Name are accepted (in the Lord's court); Nanak gives himself up to them, for ever and ever a sacrifice. O Lord, that alone is your praise which is pleasing to the Lord God; those who, through the Guru, serve the Beloved, the Lord bestows the fruit on them. Those who love the Lord: their hearts are with God; they live by repeating (the Name of) the Beloved again and again, cherishing the Lord's Name. To those who, through the Guru, have served the Beloved, I am a sacrifice; they themselves are set free, along with their families, and have set the whole world free. The beloved Guru has served the Lord; the Guru is blessed, the Guru is blessed; it is the Guru who has shown the Lord's path: great is the Guru's kindness, great kindness. The Sikhs of the Guru who serve the Guru are fortunate souls; servant Nanak gives himself up to them, for ever and ever a sacrifice. The Gurmukh companions and friends are pleasing to the Lord himself; in the Lord's court they are robed in honour; the Lord himself has taken them in his embrace. (O Lord,) grant (me) the sight of those who, through the Guru, meditate on the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered); that I may wash their feet, and stir the dust (of their feet) in water and drink it. Those (brides) who went on eating betel and areca nut, and putting rolled betel leaves in their mouths, but never remembered the Lord, Har Har: Jam (the messenger of Death) has seized them and driven them off. Those who have remembered the Name of the Lord, keeping it fixed in the heart, Jam does not come near them: (they are) the Sikhs of the Guru, dear to the Guru. The Lord's Name is a treasure; only a rare one, through the Guru, knows it. O Nanak, whoever has met the True Guru enjoys delight in (the Lord's) love. The True Guru is to be called the Giver; pleased, he grants his favour; I am ever a sacrifice to the Guru, who has given (me) the Name. Blessed is that Guru, praise be to him, who gives the Lord's message; beholding the Guru again and again, the form of the Guru, the True Guru, I have blossomed. The Guru's tongue speaks Amrit; it is lovely with the Lord's Name; the Sikhs who heard and put their faith in the Guru: all their hunger is gone. There is talk of the Lord's path; tell me, in what way is one to walk it? O Lord, Har Har, your Name (is the provision): taking the Lord's provision one should set out. Those who, through the Guru, have worshipped the Lord are rich merchants, wise indeed; I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru; through the Guru's word (they) have merged (in the Lord). You are (my) Master, you my Lord, you alone my Sovereign; if it pleases you, (then only is) your devotion (done); you are the deep sea of virtues. The Lord himself is of one form, and himself of many forms; what is pleasing to him, O Nanak, that alone is good. ॥22॥
Pirharhi: love (a word of the Lahnda, western Punjabi, speech); biri: a rolled betel leaf.
726.1: Raag Tilang Kafi, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. If you would remember (him), O mortal, then remember (him) night and day; moment by moment life slips away, like water from a cracked pot. Why do you not sing the praises of the Lord, O foolish, unknowing one? clinging to false greed, you have not recognised death. Even now nothing is lost, if one sings God's praises; says Nanak, through worship of him one attains the fearless state. ॥2॥
Kafi: this hymn is to be sung in Tilang blended with Raag Kafi.
726.2: Raag Tilang, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Wake, O mind, wake up; why do you lie asleep, heedless? the body that came into being along with (you), even that has not gone along with (you). Mother, father, sons and kinsfolk, on whom (one) set one's love, when the soul left the body, cast (it) into the fire. All dealings last only while one lives: know the world (to be so); O Nanak, sing the praises of the Lord: all (this) is like a dream. ॥2॥
727.1: Raag Tilang, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Sing the Lord's praise, O mind: it is your (true) companion; the time (of life) is slipping away: heed what I tell you. You have set great love on property, chariots, wealth and rule; when the noose of death falls on the neck, all becomes another's. Knowing and understanding (it all), O madman, you have spoilt your task; you did not shrink from sin, nor did you rid yourself of pride. Listen, O brother, to the way the Guru has taught: Nanak says it aloud: hold fast to God's refuge. ॥3॥
727.2: Raag Tilang, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. With tall talk of the Vedas and the Katebs, O brother, the heart's unrest does not go; if you still (the mind) for even a moment, Khuda (is seen) present before you. O man, seek within your heart each day; do not roam about distraught. This world is a magic show, a fair; there is nothing (in it) to hold on to. Reading falsehoods over and over, the unknowing rejoice, and wrangle in argument; the True One, the Creator, is within his creation; he is not the dark image (of Krishna). In the sky (of the mind) the river (of the Lord) flows; in it you ought to have bathed; live ever as a faqir (in devotion); put on these glasses, (and see him) present everywhere. Allah is the purest of the pure; I would doubt (it) only if there were a second (like him). O Kabir, (this) is the grace of the Gracious One: the one on whom he bestows it, knows. ॥4॥

Persian and Arabic words: Kateb (the scriptures of the Semitic faiths: the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran), iftara (overstated claims), fikar (unrest), tuk dam (a moment), karari (stillness), hajir hajur (present before one everywhere), paresani (bewilderment), sihar (magic), darog (falsehood), bekhabar (the unknowing), hak (the True One), miane (within), lahang (flows), gusal kardan bud (one ought to have bathed), fakar (the faqir's life), daim (ever), chasme (glasses), pakan pak (purest of the pure), karam (grace). Siam murat: the image of Krishna, the dark one.
727.3: Raag Tilang, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Your Name, O Sovereign, is the staff of me, the blind one; I am poor, I am lowly; your Name is (my) support. O Gracious, O Merciful, O Allah, you (alone) are rich beyond need; you are ever present, (always) before me. You are the river (of bounty), you the Giver, you are rich beyond measure; you alone give and take back; there is none other. You are the Knower, you the Seer; what thought (of you) can I offer? O Master of Nama, O Lord, you are the Forgiver. ॥3॥

Persian words: khundkar (khudavandgar, the Lord, the Sovereign), maskin (lowly), rahim (merciful), gani (rich, in need of none), dihand (giver), bisiar (very much), digar (other), binan (seeing), bakhsand (forgiving); che (Marathi): of.
727.4: O Friend, O Friend, joyful is the news of you. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice. Sweet is even the unpaid labour you set, and most high is your Name. Where have you come from? Where did you go? Where are you going? In this city of Dwarka, tell (me) truly. Fine is your turban, sweet are your words; why a Mughal in the city of Dwarka? Of many thousands of worlds (you are) the one Master; O King, the dark-hued one (Krishna) is just such (as you). (You are) lord of horses, lord of elephants, king of men; the Master of Nama is himself the Mir, himself Mukand. ॥4॥

By tradition, at Dwarka the Lord came to Namdev in the dress of a Mughal, and Namdev speaks to him as to a friend. Persian words: hale yaran (O friend), khusikhabari (joyful news), bigari (unpaid labour), ale (most high), kuja amad kuja rafti kuja me ravi (where have you come from, where did you go, where are you going), rasi bugoi (rast bugoi, tell truly), khub (fine), chandin hajar alam (many thousands of worlds), ekal khanan (the one Khan, the Master), ham chini (just such). Mukand: the giver of liberation, a name of Krishna.

721.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
I have made one plea before you, O Creator: give it your ear.
You are true, great and gracious, without flaw, the Sustainer of all.
Know it for certain, O heart: the world is a place that passes away;
Azrail has seized the hair of my head, and you, O heart, know nothing of it.
Wife, son, father, brothers: there is none among them to take my hand;
at the last, when I have fallen and the takbir (of the funeral prayer) is said, no one can keep me (here).
Night and day I roamed in craving, and dwelt on thoughts of evil;
never have I done a good deed; such is my state.
One like me is ill-starred, a backbiter, heedless, shameless and without fear;
(yet) Nanak, your servant, says to you: (may I be) the dust under the feet of your servants. ॥4॥
721.2: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Fear of you is my bhang, and my mind the pouch (that holds it);
(drunk on it) I have become one possessed, a renunciate.
My hands are my begging bowl; (my) hunger is for the sight of you;
at (your) door I beg, each day and every day.
I raise the beggar's cry for the sight of you;
I am a beggar at (your) door: put alms (in my bowl).
Saffron, flowers, musk and gold are put upon the bodies of all;
the devotees are like sandalwood; such is their nature that they make all fragrant.
Of ghee, silk and the vessel (of ghee) no one speaks (as defiled);
such is the devotee, whatever the caste he is born in.
Those who, bowed low in your Name, stay attuned to you in love:
Nanak (prays): at their door, put alms (in my bowl). ॥3॥
721.3: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
This body has been steeped in the mordant of Maya, O beloved, and then dyed in greed;
such a gown does not please my Husband; O beloved, how is the soul-bride to reach his bed?
I am a sacrifice, O Merciful One, I am a sacrifice;
I am a sacrifice to those who take your Name;
those who take your Name, to them I am ever a sacrifice.
Should the body be made the dyeing-tub, O beloved, and the madder of the Name be put in it,
and should the Dyer, the Master (himself), dye it, a colour (comes) such as was never seen.
Those whose gowns are so dyed, O beloved, have the Husband beside them.
Would that their dust were given (to me): dear one, put this prayer of Nanak's (before them).
He himself fashions, he himself dyes, he himself casts his glance of grace;
O Nanak, the soul-bride who is pleasing to her Husband, he himself enjoys. ॥4॥
722.1: Raag Tilang, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O foolish young (bride), why do you take such pride?
In your own home, why do you not delight in the Lord's love?
The Husband is near, O crazed bride; why do you search outside?
Put the fear (of God) into your eyes with the needle, as kohl, and make loving devotion your adornment.
Only then is she known as a happy soul-bride, joined (to him), when the Husband bestows his love (on her).
What can the foolish young girl do, if the bride is not pleasing to her Husband?
She may plead and lament ever so much, yet that bride does not reach the Mansion (of his presence);
without (his) grace nothing is gained, however much she runs about.
Drunk on craving, greed and pride, she is sunk in Maya;
by these ways the Husband is not found: the bride has proved foolish.
Go and ask those happy soul-brides by what ways the Husband is found.
(They answer:) whatever he does, let us accept as good, and give up cleverness and the giving of our own orders;
the One through whose love the treasure is gained, on his feet let us fix our mind;
what the Husband says, let us do; let us give him body and mind: such is the perfume to wear.
So say the happy soul-brides, O sister: by these ways the Husband is found.
When the self is lost, then the Husband is found; what other cleverness (avails)?
The day the Husband looks on her with grace, that day counts; the bride has gained the nine treasures.
She who is dear to her Husband is the happy soul-bride; O Nanak, she is held in honour by all.
Dyed in such love, drunk with Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), night and day she stays merged in love;
she alone is beautiful, lovely of form and discerning; she is called wise. ॥4॥
722.2: Raag Tilang, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As the Word of the Master comes to me, so do I make it known, O Lalo.
Leading a wedding party of sin, (Babur) has swept in from Kabul, and demands by force the gift of a bride, O Lalo.
Modesty and dharam have both gone into hiding, and falsehood goes about as the headman, O Lalo.
The qazis' and the Brahmins' part is over; Satan reads the marriage, O Lalo.
The Muslim women read their scriptures, and in their agony cry out to Khuda, O Lalo.
Hindu women of high caste and of low, and the rest: count them too in the same reckoning, O Lalo.
Wedding songs of blood are sung, O Nanak, and the saffron sprinkled is blood, O Lalo.
Nanak sings the virtues of the Master in this city of corpses; speak (you too) this sure word:
he who made (the world) set it to its pleasures; he sits apart, alone, and watches.
True is that Master, true is his justice; true is the judgement he will give: this is the sure word.
The cloth of the body will be torn to shreds, and Hindustan will remember this word.
(They) come in seventy-eight and will go in ninety-seven; another man of valour will also rise.
Nanak speaks the Word of the True One; he will proclaim the Truth: (this is) the time for Truth. ॥2॥
723.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
All have come from the Master by his Hukam (God's will and command); by his Hukam the whole (world) goes about its work.
True is the Master, true is his play; everywhere the Lord is the Owner.
Praise the True One: the Lord, the Owner, is above all;
he has no rival: of what account am I, to reckon (his worth)?
Air, water, earth and sky are the house and temple the Lord has made (for himself);
within them, O Nanak, he himself is at work; tell me, what can I count as false? ॥2॥
723.2: Raag Tilang, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one of evil mind does fruitless deeds every day, and boasts of them;
when he brings home (some gain) by trickery and lies, he thinks he has won the world.
Such a passing show is the world, yet he does not remember the Lord's Name;
in an instant all this perishing (show) is gone: O my mind, meditate on Ram.
That hour does not come to his mind, when Death, tormenting like a thorn, will come and seize him.
O Nanak, the one in whose heart (the Lord), in his grace, comes to dwell, he sets free. ॥2॥
723.3: Raag Tilang, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Out of dust and light (God) has made the world and all that is in it;
sky, earth, trees and water are the creation of Khuda.
O man, all that the eye sees will pass away;
yet the world, heedless in its craving, feeds on carrion (what is forbidden).
Like ghouls and beasts it kills unlawfully and eats carrion;
its heart is held fast in (craving's) grip, and the Almighty gives it the punishment of hell.
The father who gave you good things, brothers, court, estates and homes:
when Azrail binds you, of what use (will they be) then, at the parting?
The Pure One, Allah, knows (your) every state;
O Nanak, say your prayer in the presence of the dervishes, the servants (of God). ॥4॥
723.4: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is no other but you;
you are the Creator: what you do, that comes to pass.
Yours is the strength (we have), and in the mind is your support;
O Nanak, ever and ever repeat (the Name of) the One.
The Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), the Giver, is over all;
(O Lord,) yours is the prop, yours the support.
You alone are, and you will ever be,
beyond reach, beyond fathoming, lofty and without end.
Those who serve you have no fear and no pain;
by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, they sing (your) praises.
All that is seen is your form,
O treasure of virtues, O Govind of beauty beyond compare.
O servant (of God), remember, remember, remember him;
O Nanak, (he) is found by (his) grace alone.
I am a sacrifice to the one who has repeated (the Name);
in his company the world crosses over.
Says Nanak: O God, fulfil (my) longing;
for the dust of the Sants' feet I long. ॥4॥
724.1: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Merciful is the Master, merciful; my Master is merciful.
To every being he grants his gifts.
Why do you falter, O mortal? The Creator will protect you.
He who brought you into being gives (you) support.
He who made the earth takes care of it;
dwelling in every heart, he is the Master of hearts, the true Sustainer.
The worth of (his) creation cannot be known; he is great, and needs no one;
O man, give (him) your devotion while breath remains in your body.
(O Lord,) you are all-powerful, beyond words, beyond the senses; soul and body are your capital (in our keeping).
By your mercy (I) have found peace; ever (to you) is Nanak's prayer. ॥4॥
724.2: Raag Tilang, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Creator, (seeing) your creation, I long for (the sight of) you;
in faith and in the world you alone (are mine); you stand untouched by all creation.
In an instant you set up and pull down; wondrous are your forms.
Who can know your wonders? (You are) a lamp in the darkness.
You yourself are the Master of creation and of the world, O Allah, merciful Khuda;
how should one who worships you day and night go to hell?
Azrail is the friend of the man who has your support;
all his sins are pardoned; your servants behold the sight of you.
All the things of the world are for the moment only; your Name is the true peace.
Meeting the Guru, Nanak has understood (this); (now) I ever sing of the One alone. ॥4॥
724.3: Raag Tilang, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Chief, O Wise One, Purifier of hearts,
love (of you) dwells in (my) mind and body, O true King, O Freer of captives.
To behold the sight of you, O Master: there is no price for it at all;
you are the Pure One, the Sustainer; you yourself are the Master, great and beyond weighing.
Take my hand, O Brave One; you alone, you alone are the One.
O Creator, Maker of all nature, Fashioner of all beings: Nanak leans on you alone. ॥2॥
724.4: Raag Tilang, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
He who made (the world) has watched over it; what can one say, O brother?
He who has planted the garden himself knows, and himself acts.
(Tell) the tale of the Beloved, the tale through which there is peace for ever.
She who has not enjoyed her Husband in love, O brother, comes to repent;
wringing her hands, she beats her head, when the night (of life) is spent.
Repenting brings nothing, once (the night) is wholly gone;
then the Beloved can be enjoyed only when (her) turn comes again.
The happy soul-brides have won the Husband; they are better than I;
those virtues do not come to me; on whom, O dear one, shall I lay the blame?
I shall go and ask the friends who have enjoyed the Husband;
I will fall at their feet and entreat them, and have them tell me the way.
She who recognises the Hukam, O Nanak, and wears the fear (of God) as sandal,
the bride who makes virtues her love-charms: then she wins the Beloved.
One who has met (him) in the heart stays united; that one alone, O brother, is said to have met (him).
However much one may long, there is no union by mere talk.
Metal blends again with metal, and love runs to love;
when (this) is understood by the Guru's grace, then one attains the Fearless (Lord).
A garden of betel may grow in the home, yet the donkey knows nothing of its worth;
only when one delights in fragrance does one know the flower.
O Nanak, one who drinks the Amrit, his wandering doubt dies away within;
in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj, he stays united, and attains the deathless state. ॥10॥
725.1: Raag Tilang, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
My friend the Guru has recounted to (me) the Lord's stories and tales;
I am a sacrifice to my own Guru; to the Guru I give myself.
Come and meet me, O Sikh of the Guru, come and meet me, you beloved of my Guru.
The Lord's praises please the Lord; these (praises) I have received from the Guru.
To those who have accepted the Guru's will I am a sacrifice, again and again.
I give myself to those who have seen the beloved True Guru;
to those who have served the Guru I am ever a sacrifice.
O Lord, Har Har, your Name is the dispeller of sorrow;
it is found by serving the Guru; through the Guru comes deliverance.
Those who meditate on the Lord's Name are accepted (in the Lord's court);
Nanak gives himself up to them, for ever and ever a sacrifice.
O Lord, that alone is your praise which is pleasing to the Lord God;
those who, through the Guru, serve the Beloved, the Lord bestows the fruit on them.
Those who love the Lord: their hearts are with God;
they live by repeating (the Name of) the Beloved again and again, cherishing the Lord's Name.
To those who, through the Guru, have served the Beloved, I am a sacrifice;
they themselves are set free, along with their families, and have set the whole world free.
The beloved Guru has served the Lord; the Guru is blessed, the Guru is blessed;
it is the Guru who has shown the Lord's path: great is the Guru's kindness, great kindness.
The Sikhs of the Guru who serve the Guru are fortunate souls;
servant Nanak gives himself up to them, for ever and ever a sacrifice.
The Gurmukh companions and friends are pleasing to the Lord himself;
in the Lord's court they are robed in honour; the Lord himself has taken them in his embrace.
(O Lord,) grant (me) the sight of those who, through the Guru, meditate on the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered);
that I may wash their feet, and stir the dust (of their feet) in water and drink it.
Those (brides) who went on eating betel and areca nut, and putting rolled betel leaves in their mouths,
but never remembered the Lord, Har Har: Jam (the messenger of Death) has seized them and driven them off.
Those who have remembered the Name of the Lord, keeping it fixed in the heart,
Jam does not come near them: (they are) the Sikhs of the Guru, dear to the Guru.
The Lord's Name is a treasure; only a rare one, through the Guru, knows it.
O Nanak, whoever has met the True Guru enjoys delight in (the Lord's) love.
The True Guru is to be called the Giver; pleased, he grants his favour;
I am ever a sacrifice to the Guru, who has given (me) the Name.
Blessed is that Guru, praise be to him, who gives the Lord's message;
beholding the Guru again and again, the form of the Guru, the True Guru, I have blossomed.
The Guru's tongue speaks Amrit; it is lovely with the Lord's Name;
the Sikhs who heard and put their faith in the Guru: all their hunger is gone.
There is talk of the Lord's path; tell me, in what way is one to walk it?
O Lord, Har Har, your Name (is the provision): taking the Lord's provision one should set out.
Those who, through the Guru, have worshipped the Lord are rich merchants, wise indeed;
I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru; through the Guru's word (they) have merged (in the Lord).
You are (my) Master, you my Lord, you alone my Sovereign;
if it pleases you, (then only is) your devotion (done); you are the deep sea of virtues.
The Lord himself is of one form, and himself of many forms;
what is pleasing to him, O Nanak, that alone is good. ॥22॥
726.1: Raag Tilang Kafi, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
If you would remember (him), O mortal, then remember (him) night and day;
moment by moment life slips away, like water from a cracked pot.
Why do you not sing the praises of the Lord, O foolish, unknowing one?
clinging to false greed, you have not recognised death.
Even now nothing is lost, if one sings God's praises;
says Nanak, through worship of him one attains the fearless state. ॥2॥
726.2: Raag Tilang, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Wake, O mind, wake up; why do you lie asleep, heedless?
the body that came into being along with (you), even that has not gone along with (you).
Mother, father, sons and kinsfolk, on whom (one) set one's love,
when the soul left the body, cast (it) into the fire.
All dealings last only while one lives: know the world (to be so);
O Nanak, sing the praises of the Lord: all (this) is like a dream. ॥2॥
727.1: Raag Tilang, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Sing the Lord's praise, O mind: it is your (true) companion;
the time (of life) is slipping away: heed what I tell you.
You have set great love on property, chariots, wealth and rule;
when the noose of death falls on the neck, all becomes another's.
Knowing and understanding (it all), O madman, you have spoilt your task;
you did not shrink from sin, nor did you rid yourself of pride.
Listen, O brother, to the way the Guru has taught:
Nanak says it aloud: hold fast to God's refuge. ॥3॥
727.2: Raag Tilang, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
With tall talk of the Vedas and the Katebs, O brother, the heart's unrest does not go;
if you still (the mind) for even a moment, Khuda (is seen) present before you.
O man, seek within your heart each day; do not roam about distraught.
This world is a magic show, a fair; there is nothing (in it) to hold on to.
Reading falsehoods over and over, the unknowing rejoice, and wrangle in argument;
the True One, the Creator, is within his creation; he is not the dark image (of Krishna).
In the sky (of the mind) the river (of the Lord) flows; in it you ought to have bathed;
live ever as a faqir (in devotion); put on these glasses, (and see him) present everywhere.
Allah is the purest of the pure; I would doubt (it) only if there were a second (like him).
O Kabir, (this) is the grace of the Gracious One: the one on whom he bestows it, knows. ॥4॥
727.3: Raag Tilang, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Your Name, O Sovereign, is the staff of me, the blind one;
I am poor, I am lowly; your Name is (my) support.
O Gracious, O Merciful, O Allah, you (alone) are rich beyond need;
you are ever present, (always) before me.
You are the river (of bounty), you the Giver, you are rich beyond measure;
you alone give and take back; there is none other.
You are the Knower, you the Seer; what thought (of you) can I offer?
O Master of Nama, O Lord, you are the Forgiver. ॥3॥
727.4: O Friend, O Friend, joyful is the news of you.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice. Sweet is even the unpaid labour you set, and most high is your Name.
Where have you come from? Where did you go? Where are you going?
In this city of Dwarka, tell (me) truly.
Fine is your turban, sweet are your words;
why a Mughal in the city of Dwarka?
Of many thousands of worlds (you are) the one Master;
O King, the dark-hued one (Krishna) is just such (as you).
(You are) lord of horses, lord of elephants, king of men;
the Master of Nama is himself the Mir, himself Mukand. ॥4॥
